solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: a cricket is an insect famous for leaping
to suit something is to go well with it

explanation.surface: Someone tries on a jumper to go with a suit, maybe as a test of the outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, but it is a leaping insect. A Test is an international fixture in cricket, the bat-and-ball sport, so 'Maybe' flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is the longest international form of the bat-and-ball game, so it is one instance of such a fixture, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Deception at an end in competition

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: something over is finished
a cup is a knockout competition, like the FA Cup

explanation.surface: A cheat is discovered just as a contest finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At an end' reads as a time phrase, but it is a synonym for finished; the competition is a trophy tournament like the FA Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding the truth about wrongdoing is a classic form of trickery, the kind politicians are accused of after scandals.

clue.text: Isle is off North America, first of all

indicators.note: the first of all the words means take the opening letter of each one

blocks.note: initial letters of four consecutive words

explanation.surface: A geography fact: some island lies off the coast of North America.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is not American at all: IONA lies off western Scotland and is famous for its early Christian abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides, so it is an example of an island.

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: ken is an old word for range of understanding
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Reads like learning about a long room, perhaps a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb, to yearn, not an adjective describing the room. KEN as knowledge survives in the phrase 'beyond my ken'.
explanation.definitionFit: The place in a house where food is cooked is one particular sort of chamber in a home.

blocks.note: first meaning: revealing or meaningful, as in a revealing detail
second meaning: what an informer does, reporting someone to authority

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second definition is playful: a snitch informs on others, and that action is the noun form of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail that reveals much is called by the adjective, while informing on classmates is the noun sense of the same word.

clue.text: A girl hasn’t finished, I’m sorry to say

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
lass is a northern British word for a girl

explanation.surface: An apology that a young woman has not completed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A girl' reads as one person, but the A stands alone and the girl is a lass, a northern British word, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection expresses regret before bad news, exactly as the apologetic phrase does when announcing something unwelcome.

blocks.note: first meaning: satisfied, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: what something holds, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone happy that some fabric was added; the two meanings are pronounced differently but spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense describes satisfaction with one's lot; the other is the stuff held within a book, website or container.

clue.text: Taken by surprise when crash hit

blocks.note: a crash of noise during a storm
past tense: to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A driver is caught unawares as a car crash happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash' suggests a collision, but it is the loud clap of a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being so astonished as to be speechless is the idiomatic sense, as if felled by a bolt from the sky.

clue.text: Dreary TV a slog unfortunately – then few will watch!

indicators.note: something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A grumble that dull, laborious television drives viewers away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of a time rather than a synonym: 'then' points to a broadcasting period when audiences are tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters use the phrase for a late-night or otherwise unpopular scheduling period that attracts very small audiences.

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its insides, so only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: a haven is a place of safety
the outer letters of the old word for often

explanation.surface: A refuge often stands empty; pity the man who needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' seems to describe the sanctuary, but it works on 'oft' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase 'the haves and the have-nots', the second group are people lacking wealth, so an impoverished person.

clue.text: Ultimately, educational complex nearer for student

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the closing letter is taken
something complex is intricate and tangled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school campus is built closer to where a pupil lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Educational complex' looks like a noun phrase for a school, but 'complex' is the anagram signal working on 'nearer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone studying is someone acquiring knowledge, so the two words are straightforward synonyms.

blocks.note: a lack of something means there is none of it
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A joke that being short of marines is standard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Marines are Britain's naval infantry, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard or typical pattern is what is expected and ordinary, so the customary state of affairs.

clue.text: First of actors in hit series

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to chin someone is slang for punching them on the jaw
the opening letter

explanation.surface: The lead performer appears in a popular television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit series' looks like a successful show, but 'hit' is a verb and 'series' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A linked sequence of events or shops is called by this word, so it fits a succession of things.

indicators.note: a little of a word is only a small part of it, so the letters lie inside

blocks.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A complaint that fuel is priced a bit too low.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel used in road vehicles, from Diesel Engine Road Vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is diesel oil for lorries and cars, so it is a type of motor fuel.

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the initial letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter
an ally is a supporter or friend

explanation.surface: Advice to mend relationships, mainly by being with a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like part of the phrase 'improve relations', but it only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient or a market is said to recover strength when it picks up, so the verb means get better.

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written
EG means for example, as does 'say'

explanation.surface: A household instruction to undo the rubbish sacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bin bags' reads as rubbish sacks, but 'bags' is a verb meaning captures.
explanation.definitionFit: To start a meeting or a game is to get it under way, the verb sense of the definition.

indicators.note: something cracked is broken, so its letters come apart and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A mechanic asks to be shown the spot where a component broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a garage request, but 'Show' is the definition, as in show someone how.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate how something works is to make it clear by description, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Large empty tray shaken a lot

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its insides, so only the outside letters remain
shaking something jumbles its contents into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the outer letters

explanation.surface: A big tray with nothing on it gets rattled about considerably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' looks like a synonym to swap, but it is taken as written and joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means to a high degree, which is what the casual phrase means after a verb, as in 'improved considerably'.

indicators.note: what is visible in a picture is contained within its frame

blocks.note: a shot is a photograph
all of it, wholly

explanation.surface: A food photographer makes sure the whole vegetable is in frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Photo' is a camera shot, and 'entirely' gives a three-letter word for wholly that sits within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mild onion-like bulb used in cooking is one particular kind of vegetable.

indicators.note: in a down entry, higher means placed above, so earlier in the answer

blocks.note: 'as' can mean while, as in 'as I left'
Roman numeral one
a number

explanation.surface: A foolish figure, with a single digit raised above it.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue order is number first, but 'higher' puts the pieces for 'while' and 'one' above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from the Latin for donkey and means extremely foolish, like a stupid animal.

clue.text: Something in the 3 Down has to flower

blocks.note: taken as written
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Reads as a puzzle about what a certain room needs in order to bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 Down answer is KITCHEN, so the definition is a kitchen item.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric appliance for browning bread usually sits on a worktop where meals are cooked, an example of such equipment.

clue.text: Dieter’s back into healthier fried food!

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken
going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: fitter means in better health
the last letter

explanation.surface: A slimmer returns to a healthier regime, then celebrates with greasy food.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark marks the irony of a dieter ending up with deep-fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of fruit or vegetable dipped in batter and cooked in hot oil is a kind of fried snack.

indicators.note: beyond means further along, so this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: past tense: to experience is to feel
a tip is a hint

explanation.surface: A hint that goes over the head of a veteran author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a fibrous point used for marking is something that produces script, so it is a writing implement.

blocks.note: first meaning: a coach who teaches skills
second meaning: a sports shoe, worn on the foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'One going on foot' sounds like a walker, but it is a shoe that goes on a foot. In Britain a trainer is a sneaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitness coach teaches clients; a running shoe is pulled on over the foot, giving two separate senses.

indicators.note: being surrounded by something reads here as sitting in it, supplying the word for that position

blocks.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
to be surrounded by something is to be in it

explanation.surface: An ancient deity is encircled by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded by' looks like a container signal, but it simply supplies a two-letter word after the Egyptian god; 'water' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation falling from clouds is droplets of liquid, so the word is a specific form of that substance.

indicators.note: hugging something means wrapping arms around it

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
p is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A tree-hugger embraces a trunk gently.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The species with the leaf on Canada's flag is a deciduous broadleaf, one example of this plant group.

blocks.note: first meaning: a planet, the red one
second meaning: damages or spoils

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a lament that the world is in pain; 'World' is a planet and 'is hurting' a verb meaning spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth planet from the Sun is a world; a blemish that spoils something damages it, the present tense verb.

clue.text: 19 Down plan, right to pull out

indicators.note: pulling out means withdrawing, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a draft is a preliminary plan
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A foolish scheme, and the right to back out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 Down is ASININE, meaning silly. DRAFT loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for foolish, so it matches the earlier answer meaning stupid.

blocks.note: first meaning: press creases out of clothes
second meaning: the metal Fe

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like an instruction to crush a chemical; the verb is pressing laundry and the noun is a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing creases out of shirts uses a heated appliance; the metal Fe is number 26 on the periodic table.

clue.text: Border crossed by wagon for designs available online

indicators.note: something crossed by another has that thing passing across it, so one piece straddles the other

blocks.note: a cart is a wagon
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A wagon crosses a frontier carrying patterns sold on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests a frontier between countries, but it means an edge or rim here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made pictures that can be copied into documents are offered free on many websites, so they are graphics found on the internet.

clue.text: North American city somewhat dominant, or on top

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the text is used

blocks.note: runs from the last letter of the first word to the first two of the last

explanation.surface: A city is described as fairly powerful, or even leading.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans four words, starting at the final letter of 'dominant'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest city in Canada and capital of Ontario, so it is an example of a city on that continent.

clue.text: To whom it may concern, perhaps – is that a knife?

definitions.text: To whom it may concern, perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: To whom it may concern, perhaps
blocks.note: first meaning: the phrase that starts some formal correspondence
second meaning: a blade for slitting envelopes

explanation.walkthrough: The formal salutation is an example of how a written message begins, hence 'perhaps'; the same two words name a desk blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A salutation is how correspondence begins, while a paper knife used to slit envelopes is called by the same phrase.
